# SOTA Open-Model Serving on Google Cloud — G4 (RTX PRO 6000), GB200 and GB300

> Production-validated SGLang and vLLM recipes and measured benchmarks for serving trillion-parameter-class open models on Google Cloud G4 instances (8× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell SM120, 96 GB GDDR7, PCIe Gen 5, no NVLink, no GPU RDMA). Covers NVFP4/FP8/INT4 quantization, multi-node TP8·PP2 parallelism over plain TCP, HiCache KV-cache offload, real agentic trace-replay benchmarks, dual-NIC NCCL networking, and prefix-cache-aware routing with the GKE Inference Gateway (llm-d).

Key measured results (standard profile 1024 in / 8192 out, 512 concurrency, unless noted):
- Kimi-K2.6 NVFP4, 2 nodes: 3,261.28 output tok/s — repo best (bench_one_batch peak: 14,015.66 tok/s prefill)
- Kimi-K2.5 NVFP4, 2 nodes: 3,237.46 output tok/s
- Kimi-K3 on 4-node GB200: 2,883 total tok/s peak at concurrency 256 (1k/1k); ViBench agentic coding 95.6/100 over 24 apps on 8 nodes; ViBench Hard (brownfield feature extension, 63 test plans) 79.2/100 with 0 failed artifacts
- Kimi-K3 on 4-node G4 (32x RTX PRO 6000, PP=4 TP=8, plain VPC ethernet, no NVLink/RDMA): 583.58 output tok/s peak at concurrency 112 (1k/8k), 480.86 tok/s at concurrency 64 with zero queueing and sub-530ms median TTFT; TPOT flat at 77.7-78.8 ms/token to 128 concurrency; 51.49 ms/tok single-stream decode; weights served from a Hyperdisk ML ReadOnlyMany volume mounted across all 4 nodes; 1,104 requests, 0 failures
- Gemma-4-26B-A4B FP8 on a single RTX PRO 6000 via vLLM: 4,054.82 output tok/s peak (1k/1k @ 1024c), sub-250 ms median TTFT through concurrency 256; 24,327 total tok/s on a 10K-prompt profile — the only single-GPU LLM recipe here
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 MXFP4, 2 nodes: 4,711 output tok/s at concurrency 512 (1k/1k) with no saturation plateau; TPOT 75 → 107 ms from 1 → 512 streams
- GLM-5.2 FP8, 2 nodes (early config): 1,645.21 output tok/s; NVFP4 validated on GB300 (A4X Max)
- GLM-5.2 NVFP4, 1 node (8x RTX PRO 6000, TP8 DP8, flashinfer_cutlass MoE): 1,100.92 output tok/s at concurrency 128 = 137.6 tok/s per GPU, ~34% better per GPU than the 2-node FP8 build at less than half the TPOT (115 vs 240 ms); 461.27 output tok/s at concurrency 64 with 1.0 s median TTFT. Requires --dsa-prefill-backend trtllm --dsa-decode-backend trtllm: the auto-selected flashinfer_sparse_mla silently emits NaN logits on SM120 with fp8 KV cache
- GLM-5.3-Flash FP8, 1 node (8x RTX PRO 6000, TP8, tuned SM120 fused-MoE Triton kernels, tilelang DSA): 9,481.7 total tok/s peak on 8k/1k prefill at concurrency 128 (8,417.5 input tok/s); 2,579.8 output tok/s on 1k/8k reasoning at concurrency 256 = 322.5 tok/s per GPU without speculation; recommended envelope 64-128 concurrency with sub-second median TTFT and 30-54 ms ITL. Needs two SM120 patches to serve at all (tilelang DSA num_stages=1 for the 99 KB smem cap, tilelang DSA backend override for the rope=0 256-dim layout); DP-attention ruled out on SM120 (smem overflow, PCIe-only fabric)
- DeepSeek-V3.2 NVFP4, 1 node: 334.4 output tok/s per GPU with EAGLE speculation
- Reflection Beam-1.0 NVFP4 (501B, A23B), 1 node (8x RTX PRO 6000, TP8 EP8, flashinfer_cutlass MoE with a one-line SM120 patch, DFlash speculative decoding block 8, HiCache ratio 2.0 write_back, public lmsysorg/sglang:beam image): 6,952.86 output tok/s on 1k/8k at concurrency 128 (15.4 ms median TPOT), 13,567.5 total tok/s on 8k/1k at 128 (prefill-bound), 8.8 ms median TPOT on 1k/1k at 32. Greedy decoding with ignore_eos (accept length 7.2-7.9 of 8), so these are an upper bound for DFlash. Reflection-reported NVFP4 evals are within 1.7 points of BF16 (SWE-bench Verified 80.7 vs 81.6)
- Meta Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B NVFP4 (816B, A42B), 1 node (8x RTX PRO 6000 SM120, TP8 EP8, flashinfer_cutlass NVFP4 MoE via ConfigMap patch, DFlash speculative decoding with RadixArk/Muse-Spark-Open-DFlash2 block 8, HiCache, image aurius/sglang-muse-spark-rtxpro6000:10182026): 1,987.32 output tok/s (2,235.74 total tok/s, 3,881.0 peak output tok/s, 16.09 ms median TPOT, 14.07 ms median ITL, 7.11 avg accept length) on 1k/8k at concurrency 64; 1,925.79 output tok/s (3,851.58 total tok/s, 3,920.0 peak output tok/s, 15.92 ms median ITL, 6.97 avg accept length) on 1k/1k at concurrency 64
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (Oct 17, 2026 checkpoint), 1 node (8x RTX PRO 6000 SM120, TP8 EP8, FP4 routed experts via FlashInfer SM120 CUTLASS W4A8 MoE, FP8 dense GEMMs and fp8_e4m3 KV cache, DSPARK speculative decoding block 5, HiCache ratio 2.0 write_back, Engram host tables, 262K context, image lmsysorg/sglang:dev-dsv41 plus a ConfigMap-applied SM120 attention-kernel patch): 4,699.5 output tok/s (5,286.9 total, 5,643 peak output, 22.51 ms median TPOT, 21.0 ms median ITL, 5.28 accept length) on 1k/8k at concurrency 128; 3,217.7 output / 6,435.4 total tok/s on 1k/1k at 128; 12,851.3 total tok/s (11,423 input tok/s) on 8k/1k at 128; median ITL 9 / 13 / 21 ms at concurrency 32 / 64 / 128 for every shape. The stock image's per-(token, head) Triton sparse-MLA kernel was 54 % of decode and 67 % of prefill GPU time; the MQA-tiled tensor-core replacement is 8-11x faster and equal to bf16 rounding, giving 1.85-2.67x throughput and about 2x lower latency over the stock configuration (1,817 / 4,816 / 2,661 on the same runs). AgentX 256K agentic replay at C=16 (stock build): 295 requests, 0 errors, 742 ms median TTFT, 26.8 ms median ITL, 94.7 % prompt-cache hit rate
- Agentic trace replay (12,542 real requests, up to 250 steps, ~73K-token prompts): 81.2% prefix-cache hit rate on a single node
- HiCache on Qwen3.5-397B with 20K-token prompts: P99 TTFT 14.05 s → 3.36 s
- NCCL AllReduce across two nodes on plain TCP via dual 200 Gbps NICs: ~38 GB/s (~303 Gbps)

## Documentation

- [Interactive docs site](https://shivajid.github.io/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/): full benchmark tables, per-model recipes, hardware/NUMA topology, networking results, and an interactive GKE Inference Gateway simulator
- [Repository README](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/blob/main/README.md): summary benchmark table and key updates

## Model recipes and results

- [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/DeepSeekV4.1-Flash-1017): single-node G4 recipe (8x RTX PRO 6000 SM120, TP8 EP8) with FP4 routed experts, FP8 dense/KV, DSPARK speculative decoding, HiCache, Engram host tables and 262K context; ConfigMap-delivered SM120 attention-kernel patch (MQA-tiled tensor-core sparse-MLA decode kernel, 8-11x faster than stock) with the stock-kernel manifest kept for A/B; 9-run ISL/OSL sweep at concurrency 32-128 with charts and stock-vs-patched comparison; AgentX 256K agentic replay Job and results
- [Meta Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/Meta-Muse-Spark): NVFP4 single-node recipe (8x RTX PRO 6000 SM120, TP8 EP8) with DFlash speculative decoding (RadixArk/Muse-Spark-Open-DFlash2), HiCache, SM120 CUTLASS NVFP4 MoE ConfigMap patch, slimmed 27.7 GB image (aurius/sglang-muse-spark-rtxpro6000:10182026), and C=64 1k/1k & 1k/8k benchmarks
- [Kimi-K2.6](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/KimiK2.6): EAGLE3 speculation + HiCache + GCS Fuse weights; NVFP4 2-node config (repo's best throughput) and bench_one_batch results
- [Kimi-K2.5](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/KimiK2.5): INT4 vs NVFP4 head-to-head on 16 GPUs with DP8 attention
- [DeepSeek-V3.2](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/DeepSeekV3.2): NSA attention, EAGLE speculation; 1-node NVFP4 vs 2-node FP8 trade-offs
- [DeepSeek-V4-Flash](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/DeepSeekV4-Flash-0731): 0731 checkpoint, MXFP4 MoE runner, 2-node concurrency sweep 1→512 with charts; unoptimized 1.6T DeepSeek-V4-Pro config in models/DeepSeekv4
- [Kimi-K3](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/kimik3): GB200 LeaderWorkerSet configs (TP16·DCP16 / TP32·DCP32), concurrency sweep 1→512 with charts, ViBench agentic coding reports
- [Kimi-K3 on G4](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/kimik3/g4): 4-node RTX PRO 6000 recipe — PP=4·TP=8, marlin MoE with SM120 patch, triton radix linear attention, HiCache host-RAM spillover, fp8_e4m3 KV cache, 128K context, Hyperdisk ML weight provisioning guide
- [GLM-5.1](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/GLM5.1): NEXTN speculation; super-linear 1→2 node scaling under saturation
- [GLM-5.2](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/GLM5.2): NVFP4 single-node G4 recipe (Hyperdisk ML weights, GSM8K correctness gate, DSA backend fixes), FP8 2-node G4 results, and GB300 (A4X Max) NVFP4 single-host setup guide
- [GLM-5.3-Flash](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/GLM5.3-Flash): single-node FP8 recipe with custom-tuned SM120 fused-MoE Triton kernel config (E=289), 12-run concurrency sweep across 1k/1k, 1k/8k and 8k/1k workloads, torch.profiler kernel breakdown (NCCL AllReduce ~43% on PCIe) and optimization roadmap
- [Qwen3.5-397B](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/Qwen3.5): HiCache latency A/B with 20K-token prompts
- [Reflection Beam-1.0](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/Reflection-Beam): NVFP4 single-node recipe with DFlash speculative decoding and HiCache on the public lmsysorg/sglang:beam image (SM120 MoE-runner patch as a ConfigMap, weights downloaded at launch onto a 500 GiB Hyperdisk Balanced ephemeral volume), 9-run ISL/OSL sweep at concurrency 32-128 with chart, Reflection's published NVFP4 vs BF16 evals, and an AgentX long-context HiCache report
- [Gemma-4-26B](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/Gemma4-26B): single-GPU vLLM FP8 recipe, concurrency sweep 32→1024 across four workload shapes, plus a 10K-context 1-GPU vs TP=2 comparison
- [Whisper-large-v3](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/Whisper): DP8 audio transcription, 55.6 req/s
- [Chandra-OCR-2](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/ChandraOCR): single-GPU vision OCR, fastest TPOT in the repo (32.5 ms)

## Agentic harness

- [Gemini CLI + SGLang](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/sglang_gemini_cli): point the Gemini CLI at any SGLang OpenAI-compatible `/v1` endpoint via three environment variables (SGLANG_BASE_URL, GEMINI_MODEL, GEMINI_DEFAULT_AUTH_TYPE) to get a self-hosted coding agent with file edits and shell execution; validated with Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731; requires Node >= 20, run with `npx @shivajidnpm2026/gemini-cli`
- [Harness setup guide on the docs site](https://shivajid.github.io/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/#geminicli): install, network path (direct pod IP vs kubectl port-forward), endpoint verification, environment variables, troubleshooting

## GKE Inference Gateway (llm-d)

- [Inference Gateway recipes](https://github.com/shivajid/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/tree/main/models/KimiK2.6/gke-inference-gateway): prefix-cache-aware routing for SGLang and vLLM backends — Gateway API, InferencePool, Endpoint Picker (EPP); the EPP is a control-plane ext-proc that returns routing decisions and never carries traffic
- [llm-d project](https://llm-d.ai): the upstream framework for cache-aware LLM routing on Kubernetes

## Optional

- [Model chooser](https://shivajid.github.io/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/#chooser): qualitative guide to which model fits which use case (interactive scale, agentic workloads, long context, RAG latency, single-node budgets, ASR, OCR)

- [Agentic benchmark details](https://shivajid.github.io/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/#agentic): trace-replay methodology, HiCache + longest-prefix-match scheduling, single-node vs two-node latency findings
- [Networking (DRANET dual-NIC)](https://shivajid.github.io/sglang-rtx-pro-6000/#network): iperf3 and NCCL results over jumbo-frame VPC
